hypothesis: The empirical RECOMB_BOOST=2.0 knob (no first-principles basis) is load-bearing for the chemistry G-values reported vs Geant4 chem6. Test: re-run with the knob at its neutral value 1.0 and report the parameter-free yields.
method: Set RECOMB_BOOST=1.0 in src/shaders/helpers.wgsl (SIGMA_EXC_SCALE kept at 0.5), regenerated the 10 keV rad_buf dump via experiments/lib/regenerate-dumps.mjs (Phase A+B, chemistry disabled), then ran the IRT worker (tools/run_irt.cjs, n_therm=4096, E=10000) on the new dump. Production state (RECOMB_BOOST=2.0, dumps) restored afterward; this is a sensitivity measurement, not a production change.
finding: The RECOMB_BOOST knob is NOT load-bearing. Removing it (2.0 -> 1.0) changes the 5-species RMS deviation vs chem6 at 1 us by only ~1.4 pp (18.3% -> 19.7%). Per species, removing it IMPROVES OH (0.895->0.914), eaq (0.814->0.858), and H (eliminates the 1.096x overshoot -> 0.928x), and WORSENS only H2 (0.863->0.741); H2O2 unchanged (0.693x). The knob mainly props up G(H2) at the cost of an H overshoot. Conclusion: the parameter-free yields are reportable as the primary chemistry result with negligible loss of overall agreement, removing the need for the unphysical knob in the paper.
note: Larger dump at RECOMB=1.0 (84.5 vs 79.5 MB) = more radicals survive (less recombination), as expected.
